ACCEPTThe clarifications repair the defects identified in the previous audit. The new diagonal-chain classification is also correct under the stated row/column convention. The earlier objection to the private repair was caused by reversing the coordinate axes; with coordinates  $(\text{row},\text{column})$ , that objection does not apply.This acceptance is for the written theorem and its stated conditional scope. It does not assert the still-open universal grid compensation theorem.1. Reservations and the identity  $|F|=D-2L$ Let  $n_1$  be the number of deficient tiles in  $R$  with  $t=1$ . Since deficient tiles have  $t\in\{0,1\}$ ,
$$\sum_{\text{deficient }U\subseteq R} b(U)=D+n_1.$$
The clarified policy reserves exactly:one baseline blank in each of those  $n_1$  tiles;two additional cap blanks in each of the  $L$  marked tiles.The clarification explicitly makes the marked  $t=1$  baseline equal to the pressure-forced other noncap corner, rather than reserving that corner again. It also states that baseline and cap reservations are disjoint as actual vertices. Therefore the number of remaining deficient-tile blanks is
$$|F|
=(D+n_1)-n_1-2L
=D-2L.$$
The previous concern about an arbitrary marked  $t=1$  baseline choice and possible overlap with a cap blank has therefore been removed.2. Witness multiplicity and the conditional Hall theoremThe geometric degree bound is correct.A free blank  $z$  is a corner of its deficient tile. Two of its four grid neighbors are internal to that tile. Only its two external orthogonal neighbors can be selected corners of saturated tiles, and those two neighbors lie in distinct neighboring tiles. Consequently,
$$\deg_A(z)\le 2.$$
The Hall argument is also correct under the now-explicit hypothesis
$$\deg_F(S)\ge2
\qquad\text{for every }S\in A.$$
For  $X\subseteq A$ ,
$$2|X|
\le \sum_{z\in N(X)}\deg_A(z)
\le 2|N(X)|,$$
so  $|N(X)|\ge|X|$ , and Hall gives an injection from  $A$  into  $F$ .The theorem now correctly presents the left-degree condition as an assumption/certificate. It does not claim that geometry alone supplies it. This is the right scope: boundary effects, reservations, saturated neighboring tiles, and witnesses outside  $R$  can still reduce  $\deg_F(S)$  to zero or one.The parity refinement remains valid. From
$$D\equiv j+Q\equiv j+k+\eta\pmod 2$$
we obtain
$$D-(2L+k)\equiv j+\eta\pmod2,$$
and therefore
$$2\rho(R)
\le -2L+\sigma-\bigl((j+\eta)\bmod2\bigr).$$
3. Source aggregation and single-use resourcesThe clarified source domain is sufficient.The regions  $R,U_1,\ldots,U_m$  are pairwise tile-disjoint, charges are evaluated in the original full configuration, and the only witness graph is the one for  $R$ . Thus no source region receives a second allocation from  $F$ , and no blank in  $F$  is consumed once per source.Using
$$2\rho(R)=-2L+\sigma+c-d-p-u$$
and
$$\sum_i\rho(U_i)\le L,$$
additivity gives
$$\begin{aligned}
2\rho(R\cup U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_m)
&=2\rho(R)+2\sum_i\rho(U_i)\\
&\le
\bigl(-2L+\sigma+c-d-p-u\bigr)+2L\\
&=\sigma+c-d-p-u.
\end{aligned}$$
This is an arithmetic source aggregation statement. It does not claim that a witness blank from  $R$  is reassigned to a source region, and it does not independently run the allocation theorem on each  $U_i$ . The clarification correctly distinguishes this from the invalid operation of applying two local witness assignments to the same physical blank.4. The shared-corner displacement lemmaThe coordinate table is correct.With tile  $(r,c)$  having corners
$$(2r,2c),\ (2r,2c+1),\ (2r+1,2c),\ (2r+1,2c+1),$$
the external neighbors of a selected corner force the other owner as follows:
$$\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{corner of }S & S'-S & \text{corner of }S'\\
\hline
\mathrm{TL} & (-1,-1) & \mathrm{BR}\\
\mathrm{TR} & (-1,+1) & \mathrm{BL}\\
\mathrm{BL} & (+1,-1) & \mathrm{TR}\\
\mathrm{BR} & (+1,+1) & \mathrm{TL}
\end{array}$$
For example, if  $S.\mathrm{TL}=(2r,2c)$ , the two possible external neighbors are
$$(2r-1,2c)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(2r,2c-1).$$
In either case, the other external neighbor of the deficient tile lies at
$$(2r-1,2c-1),$$
which is  $S'.\mathrm{BR}$  for  $S'=(r-1,c-1)$ .The other three cases follow by reflection. Boundary vertices only remove possible witnesses; they do not create additional displacement types.5. Straight diagonal-chain classificationThe classification theorem follows from the table.If an owner has selected corners  $\mathrm{TL}/\mathrm{BR}$ , then every shared-blank edge moves by either
$$(-1,-1)\quad\text{or}\quad(+1,+1),$$
so  $c-r$  is invariant. Every neighboring owner has the same selected-corner orientation.If an owner has selected corners  $\mathrm{TR}/\mathrm{BL}$ , then every edge moves by either
$$(-1,+1)\quad\text{or}\quad(+1,-1),$$
so  $c+r$  is invariant, again preserving orientation.Thus a connected component lies on one fixed tile diagonal, and all its owners have the same orientation. Along that diagonal, an edge always joins consecutive row coordinates. A finite connected subset is therefore an interval, so after parallel edges are collapsed the underlying simple graph is a finite path, possibly a singleton.Consequently:there is no simple cycle of length at least three;the only multigraph cycles are two-edge parallel pairs;each owner pair has multiplicity at most two.The argument also correctly distinguishes shared-blank components from unrelated physical matching paths. A turn in the matching-edge geometry does not turn the shared-blank component, because the two graphs encode different incidences.6. Exact component balance and allocationSince the underlying simple graph is a path, if  $v=k$  and  $c$  is the number of components, then the number of single underlying links is  $v-c$ . If  $d$  links are doubled, then
$$e=v-c+d.$$
Therefore
$$\mu=e-v+c=d.$$
Substituting into the preceding component identity gives
$$2\rho(R)
=-2L+\sigma+c-d-p-u.$$
This is correct.The allocation characterization is also correct:a private blank allows a rooted-chain assignment;a double link supplies two distinct blanks for the two endpoints, after which the remaining chain vertices can be assigned along the path;a single-link chain with no private blank has  $v-1$  incident blanks for  $v$  owners and therefore leaves exactly one owner unmatched.The double-link argument retains the physical identity of the two blanks. It does not collapse a pair of parallel edges into one abstract edge.The condition
$$d+p+u\ge c+\sigma$$
is a valid aggregate signed-charge condition. It is a ledger statement; it does not assert that a blank in one disconnected component can be physically assigned to an owner in another component. The theorem explicitly preserves that distinction.7. The private and cycle repairsThe previous private-repair objection was incorrect under the clarified coordinates.The staircase edge
$$S_i.\mathrm{BR}\;-\;W_i.\mathrm{TR}$$
forces the first tile coordinate to be the row coordinate, because  $W_i$  is one row below  $S_i$ . Therefore
$$V=(0,a)$$
is above
$$S_0=(1,a).$$
For the private repair: $V.\mathrm{BR}=(1,2a+1)$ ; $S_0.\mathrm{TR}=(2,2a+1)$ .Thus  $V.\mathrm{BR}$  is directly adjacent to  $S_0.\mathrm{TR}$ , making it a private witness for  $S_0$ . The other external neighbor of  $V.\mathrm{BR}$  is not a selected corner of another saturated tile.Meanwhile,
$$V.\mathrm{TR}=(0,2a+1)$$
is matched to its immediate right neighbor
$$(0,2a+2),$$
which is outside  $S_0$ . It is not  $S_0.\mathrm{TL}$ , so no second occupied neighbor is introduced at  $S_0.\mathrm{TR}$ .The  $a=2$  coordinates confirm this directly:
$$V.\mathrm{BR}=(1,5),\qquad S_0.\mathrm{TR}=(2,5),$$
while the new matching endpoint is  $(0,6)$ , not  $S_0.\mathrm{TL}=(2,4)$ .The added private-repair tile has
$$t=0,\quad b=1,\quad h=1,\quad s=0,\quad d=1,$$
so
$$r=1,\qquad \rho=\frac12-1=-\frac12.$$
The cycle repair is likewise valid: its new  $V.\mathrm{BR}$  is a second distinct physical blank joining the same consecutive owner pair, producing a genuine parallel double link.8. Arbitrarily many double linksFor
$$S_i=(1+i,a-i),\qquad
W_i=(2+i,a-i),$$
the original blanks  $W_i.\mathrm{TL}$  form the single-link diagonal chain.For  $i\in I$ , the added tile
$$V_i=(1+i,a-i-1)$$
has blank  $V_i.\mathrm{BR}$ , adjacent to  $S_i.\mathrm{BL}$  and  $S_{i+1}.\mathrm{TR}$ . It therefore supplies a second edge for the owner pair  $(S_i,S_{i+1})$ .The coordinate formulas show:the first new matching-edge family has distinct even columns;the second has distinct odd columns;the two families cannot share endpoints by column parity;the new endpoints avoid all original endpoints and selected vertices;the external endpoint of each  $V_i.\mathrm{TR}$  lies in an otherwise deficient, all-blank tile.Each added tile contributes
$$t=0,\quad b=1,\quad h=1,\quad s=0,\quad d=1,$$
and hence charge  $-\tfrac12$ . The original staircase has charge  $\tfrac12$ , so for  $R_I$ ,
$$\rho(R_I)=\frac{1-|I|}{2}.$$
The component has  $a$  owners,  $a-1+|I|$  shared blanks, one connected path component, and
$$d=|I|,\qquad
c=1,\qquad
p=u=0.$$
Thus
$$2\rho(R_I)=1-|I|,$$
exactly as claimed. The double links are independent physical resources, not repeated uses of one abstract certificate.Final assessmentThe clarified theorem is internally consistent:the reservation cardinality is now justified;the Hall theorem has the necessary explicit hypothesis;source aggregation no longer reuses  $F$ ;the displacement table is correct;every shared-blank component is a straight diagonal chain;multiplicity is at most two;the only cycles are parallel pairs;the exact charge identity reduces  $\mu$  to the number of double links;both all- $a$  repairs are feasible in row/column coordinates;the arbitrary-subset construction gives the claimed family of independent double links.The remaining limitations are correctly stated: the graph classification does not prove compensation for every mixed-direction grid core, and the graph/cardinality formalization remains written rather than fully Lean-verified. Those are scope limitations, not defects in the clarified theorem.
